ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it); the child is cast aged 6 (the text: "though (he/she) is six")

collection.description: A child asks an elder how old they are, and the elder realizes they do not know: let the child guess, or pick one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) has asked (subject) how old (subject.he/she) is, and (subject) has realized (subject.he/she) doesn't know. Not exactly. (subject.He/She) knows roughly. (subject.He/She) knows it's quite a lot. But somewhere along the way (subject.he/she) stopped counting, and now (friend) is waiting for a number.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "Guess," says (subject). (friend) looks at (subject.him/her) very carefully. "A hundred?" "Lower." "Ninety-nine?" "Much lower." This goes on for some time, with (friend) getting closer by ones. When (friend.he/she) reaches a number (subject) likes the sound of, (subject) says, "That's it! Exactly that." (friend) is extremely proud of (friend.him/her)self.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) thinks about it, then picks one: a nice round number that seems about right. "That one," (subject.he/she) says. "Is that true?" asks (friend). "It is now." (friend) seems to find this a perfectly reasonable way to have an age. Later (friend.he/she) tells the other children (friend.he/she) is going to pick (friend.his/her) own, too. (friend.He/She) picks eleven, though (friend.he/she) is six.
